_about: The steps of a walk-in's visit (see CustomerManager): waiting at the host stand, being led to a table, the drink order, the drink, the food order, eating, the bill. Townsfolk say one of these lines at each step ({drink}, {dish} fill in). Regulars use their own lines from their character file instead (events seating, drink_order, drink_served, served, farewell). Done eating, a customer asks for the bill (bill) and shows a receipt over their head until it comes. A chef can chat with a regular or townsfolk while they eat. Townsfolk say the host stand, drink order, drink arriving, food order, food arriving, asking for the bill and paying in a dialogue box, the rest in a speech bubble. regular_stay_seconds: a regular who hasn't been chatted with stays this long after their food arrives before asking for the bill, saying a get_going line get_going_warning_seconds before. delivery_question: what a townsfolk asks at the bill once the restaurant has been open delivery_question_day days, which puts a phone on the wall the next morning; phone_installed is the news that morning.
_pay_scale: Every price (dish and drink base_price) times this when a customer or delivery pays: lower to make money come slower.
_walk_in_eating_seconds: How long townsfolk and other walk-ins (not regulars, see data/regulars.json eating_seconds) take over their food before they ask for the bill.
_trays: How many drinks or plates a chef can carry at once: the drink tray is there from the start, the food tray (1 = none) comes from the shop. Upgrades add to these with a drink_tray or food_tray bonus (data/upgrades.json).
delivery_question: Do you deliver? I'd order every night if you did.
phone_installed: A phone was put up on the wall last night. Customers can call in delivery orders now, and once the dinner rush is over, the night shift takes calls.
_townsfolk: What townsfolk (not regulars) say at each step, one picked at random. served_<tier> fits how the dish came out (perfect, great, okay, burnt), falling back to served; eating is their bubble while they eat, by the same tiers.

drink_order: I'll have a {drink} while I look.
served_perfect: Wow, look at that! It's perfect!
This looks too good to eat!
served_burnt: Is it... supposed to be this dark?
wrong_drink: Oh, that's not what I asked for... it's fine.
bill: I'm all done. The bill, please!

_semi_regulars: Named townsfolk (data/townsfolk/, see Townsfolk and TownsfolkTalk). season_line_chance, last_meal_line_chance and eating_choice_chance are how often those lines come up; playful_miss_chance is how often a gamble like Odette's misses; away_real_days is how long before they mention you being closed. pair_chance: how often someone from their pairs walks in right behind them (if they're in town and haven't been in today); friend_line_chance: how often an eating line is a mention of a friend you've met (see TownsfolkFriends). Who walks in is one of those in town (not been yet today), else someone already met comes in again (Townsfolk.pick_again). Anyone with no model is a plain body in their color. in_town: how many non-residents live here at once; visits_per_day: at most this many different ones come in a day (after that, someone already met comes in again: never a stranger), new_per_day of those someone never served before, so the town is met a few at a time; most_visits_each: nobody comes in more than this many times a day while someone else could (if everyone has, whoever has been in least comes back anyway, so a rush never goes empty); stay_days and away_days: [min, max] days one stays before moving away, and is away before they can come back. favorite_chance: how often they order their favorite dish or drink when it can be had. moved_in and moved_away are the morning news ({name}).
regular_get_going: I should get going soon. Just finishing up.
_guide: The Guide's arrow for new chefs: one per player, pointing the walking way to their next step, with a line at the bottom of their view (hints, by step; {name}, {verb}, {station} and {dish} are filled in). Shown to a new chef (until they've finished their first customer, or worked a shift), or to everyone with the Guide arrow setting. A new chef's first customer is followed through the whole visit (the wait_ hints show, with no arrow, while there's nothing to do for them), then a box in their view says lesson_done_title and lesson_done, with a chime, until they press on, and the arrow's gone for them from then on.

guide.lesson_done: Now on to the rest of the customers! You know the way now, so you're on your own from here.

_floor_care: Messes on the floor (FloorCare): chances (0..1) that a dish cooked well or badly leaves a spill, chopping leaves peelings, a customer leaves crumbs; most at once during a meal; seconds of one chef cleaning each. When a meal's customers have all gone, there are topped up to end_base + end_per_player for each chef. All clean when the bell is rung: clean_bonus, plus each for every one cleaned that meal. Wording is a placeholder.
_break: The breather between meals (MealBreak): a staff meal on this table's spot (or any clean one); whoever eats it moves at this much their usual speed for the next meal. Wording is a placeholder.

break.text: Breather! There's a staff meal on the table. Ring the bell when you're ready.
break.all_text: Everyone's had their staff meal. Ring the bell when you're ready!

_table_spots: How each table's spot is marked on its customers' tickets and over their heads (TableSpot): a name, a color and a shape (circle, square, triangle, diamond, pentagon, hexagon).
_takeout: The takeout counter (TakeoutCounter): a cooked dish has to be bagged here before the courier takes it, or before it can be given as a gift. After hours, free hands can also pack something from the pantry, or order a dish to go (its ticket goes in your pocket, and it's cooked the usual way). A bag can be unpacked again. per_page: choices shown at once.

takeout.nothing: (The pantry's empty, and the kitchen's closed for orders. Try cooking something to go.)

_secrets: Things a regular hides in the chair they sat in, when they say a line with "hides" (CustomerManager, Seat). Once it's hidden, a glint shows on that chair; a chef with free hands can look and find it, for the reward in money. prompt is what the chair says, found the message ({chef} fills in).

lucky_coin.found: {chef} found something wedged into the chair: Cheddar's lucky coin! (+$10)
